corrections: Discovery Loop announcement is August 5, 2026. Four founders are Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le and Oriol Vinyals. Public benefit corporation is not equivalent to nonprofit charity; scientific automation is an objective, not demonstrated universal capability.

Stanford personal page, Fulbright biography and Wikipedia introductory paragraph retain older Google roles; do not use these as current employment evidence after the 2026 transition. Historical educational and supervisory details remain independently usable.

Fulbright USA confirms ANU Bachelor of Software Engineering with First Class Honors and Stanford Computer Science PhD. Exact ANU attendance years vary across secondary accounts and are omitted. Stanford personal page identifies Alex Smola and Andrew Ng. No unverified degree-conferral date.
All seven paper timeline dates are first arXiv submissions, not conference presentations, revision dates, product releases or dates of invention.

Chain-of-thought paper first submitted January 28, 2022; nine listed authors include Jason Wei, Xuezhi Wang, Dale Schuurmans, Maarten Bosma, Brian Ichter, Fei Xia, Ed Chi, Quoc Le and Denny Zhou. Later version January 10, 2023 is not the original date. Claims limited to evaluated reasoning tasks, not guaranteed faithful reasoning or general intelligence.

AutoML-Zero first submitted March 6, 2020, with Esteban Real, Chen Liang, David R. So and Quoc V. Le. Evolutionary search over basic mathematical operations remains a research setup; no claim that all human choices or inductive biases are eliminated.
EfficientNet first submitted May 28, 2019, coauthored by Mingxing Tan and Quoc V. Le. Compound scaling coordinates depth, width and resolution. No universal hardware speed guarantee.

Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning first submitted November 5, 2016, coauthored by Barret Zoph and Quoc V. Le. Recurrent controller generates architectures and reinforcement learning optimizes validation results. Not sole invention of all AutoML.

Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks first submitted September 10, 2014, by Ilya Sutskever, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc V. Le. LSTM encoder-decoder and English–French experiments; not Transformer invention or a claim of every translation product launch.

Distributed Representations of Sentences and Documents first submitted May 16, 2014, by Quoc V. Le and Tomas Mikolov. Paragraph Vector learns fixed-length representations from variable-length text; not sole invention of word2vec.

Building High-level Features Using Large Scale Unsupervised Learning first submitted December 29, 2011, although widely reported in 2012. Eight authors include Ranzato, Monga, Devin, Chen, Corrado, Dean and Ng alongside Le. Unlabeled feature learning demonstrated face, cat-face and body features; downstream ImageNet classification also used labels. 16,000 CPU cores across 1,000 machines is not 16,000 machines. Avoid human-understanding or general-intelligence claims.
